references.text: In Genesis, Sabbath-breakers were taken outside the camp to be stoned. A similar pattern of taking someone outside the city to punish them.
The one who blasphemed God's name was led outside the camp. The people of Nazareth took Jesus outside the city, reflecting this pattern of removing a person from the community for alleged blasphemy.
Naboth was taken outside the city and stoned—a parallel to the people of Nazareth taking Jesus outside the city with the intent to kill him.
Amaziah threw prisoners off a cliff. This recalls the intention in Luke 4:29, where the crowd wanted to throw Jesus down from a precipice.
Stephen was driven outside the city to be stoned—a clear parallel to how Jesus was taken outside Nazareth with the intent to kill him.
In John 8:59, the crowd tried to stone Jesus, but he escaped—a similar pattern where Jesus escapes an attempt on his life.
The Jews picked up stones again to stone Jesus and tried to seize him, but he got away. Parallel to Luke 4:29-30.
The immediate continuation: Jesus walked right through the crowd and went on his way—he miraculously escaped their attempt to kill him.
Jesus suffered outside the city gate—a theological parallel to being taken outside the city in Nazareth.
